     RESPONSE OF VIVIAN KENDRICK, ON BEHALF OF JADENYX LP TO SOAH
      ORDER NO. 6 SHOWING GOOD CAUSE FOR FAILURE TO TIMELY FILE
     TESTIMONY OR STATEMENT OF POSITION AND REQUEST FOR HEARING

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

       Vivian Kendrick, on behalf of Jadenyx LP (“Intervenor”), an intervenor in the above-
captioned proceeding, files this Response to SOAH Order No. 6 pursuant to the procedure set forth
in that order, which provides that an intervenor who fails to file direct testimony or a statement of
position by May 13, 2026 may, by May 20, 2026, file a response setting forth good cause for
failing to comply and requesting a hearing on that issue. In support, Intervenor respectfully shows
the following:

                                       I. BACKGROUND

1.     On March 26, 2026, Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA
Transmission Services Corporation (“LCRA TSC,” and, together with Oncor, “Applicants”) filed
a joint application to amend their certificates of convenience and necessity for the Bell County
East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV transmission line project.




                                                -1-
 2.      Intervenor is an affected landowner whose property is located at or near 6215 County Road
211 in Florence, Burnet County, Texas which is crossed by or located within 500 feet of one or
more proposed transmission line routes in this proceeding.

3.      Intervenor was granted intervention by SOAH Order No. 14, issued on May 15, 2026.

4.      SOAH Order No. 6, issued April 20, 2026, established May 13, 2026 as the deadline for
intervenors to file direct testimony or a statement of position, and further provided that an
intervenor who fails to timely file such a document will be dismissed unless the intervenor files a
response by May 20, 2026 setting forth good cause and requesting a hearing on the issue.

5.      On May 19, 2026, Applicants filed a Corrected List of Intervenors Who Did Not File
Testimony or a Statement of Position, which identifies Intervenor as a party who did not timely
file by the May 13, 2026 deadline.

6.      Intervenor timely files this Response to demonstrate good cause for the failure to file direct
testimony or a statement of position by May 13, 2026, and respectfully requests a hearing on the
issue so that Intervenor may continue to participate in this proceeding.

                    II. GOOD CAUSE FOR FAILURE TO TIMELY FILE

7.      Good cause exists to excuse Intervenor’s failure to file direct testimony or a statement of
position by May 13, 2026, for the following reasons:

I tried to file testimony on the night of May 13th the deadline date. I was granted Intervenor status,
SOAH order no. 14 issued on May 15, 2026. Despite the tight deadline to file testimony, it was
completed on May 13th. However, once we (and a group of us at the same place) tried to file it
online, we couldn't get it to go through. We tried for hours through the night, and eventually
getting through the next day.

8.      Intervenor has acted in good faith throughout this proceeding and the failure to timely file
was not the result of any intent to delay these proceedings, lack of diligence, or disregard for the
orders of this tribunal.




                                                 -2-
 9.     No party will be materially prejudiced by allowing Intervenor a brief opportunity to file
testimony or a statement of position. The hearing on the merits is not scheduled to begin until June
8, 2026.

10.    Intervenor’s continued participation is important because Intervenor’s property would be
directly affected by the proposed transmission line. Dismissal would deprive Intervenor of the
ability to present evidence regarding the direct impact on my property, interruption of ranch
operations, habitable structures, Agricultural operations, community impact, etc.

           III. PROPOSED STATEMENT OF POSITION / DIRECT TESTIMONY

11.    Concurrently with this Response, Intervenor submits as Exhibit A the proposed Direct
Testimony that Intervenor seeks leave to file.

                                IV. REQUEST FOR HEARING

12.    Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6, Intervenor respectfully requests a hearing on the issue of
good cause for the late filing so that Intervenor may be heard before being dismissed as a party to
this proceeding.

                                           V. PRAYER

For the foregoing reasons, Intervenor respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges:

       (a) Find that Intervenor has shown good cause for failing to timely file direct testimony or
       a statement of position by May 13, 2026;

       (b) Grant a hearing on the issue of good cause;

       (c) Permit Intervenor to file the attached Statement of Position or Direct Testimony, or
       alternatively to file such a document within a reasonable time set by the ALJs;

       (d) Decline to dismiss Intervenor as a party to this proceeding; and

       (e) Grant Intervenor such other and further relief to which Intervenor may be entitled.

                                      PERSONAL INFORMATION

Q. Please state your name and address.
A. My name is Vivian Kendrick. My address is 6215 County Road 211, Florence, Texas 76527.
Q. Are you an intervenor in this proceeding? If so, please explain how.
A. Yes. I previously filed a Request for Intervenor Status on April 24, 2026, on behalf of Jadenyx LP.
Jadenyx LP is the owner of the family ranch (also known as the VB Ranch or Kendrick Ranch) along
County Road 211 in Burnet County. The property is affected by both the G31 Link at the front entrance
corridor and the G9 Link along the back (north) property line of the ranch.
Q. Please state your familiarity with the property.
A. My husband Barry Kendrick and I purchased the property in 2003. We are the sole principal owners of
Jadenyx LP, which holds title. The ranch is our primary residence and our home. I have personal, day-to-
day knowledge of the property, its boundaries, its structures, its wildlife operations, its water resources, and
its history.
Q. Are you testifying on your own or on behalf of another entity?
A. I am testifying on my own behalf and on behalf of Jadenyx LP, the owner of the property. My husband,
Barry Kendrick, and I are the sole principals of Jadenyx LP.
Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?
A. The purpose of my testimony is to oppose the inclusion of the G31 Link and the G9 Link in any
transmission route approved by the Commission for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation
765-kV Transmission Line Project across the Jadenyx LP property in Burnet County, and to document the
specific impacts those links would have on six contiguous Burnet County parcels we own: 54987, 54988,
and 67779 (affected by G31) and 68020, 68021, and 68022 (affected by G9).
Q. What is your overall concern with the proposed routing across your property?
A. My overall concern is that the proposed G31 and G9 alignments together pin our ranch between two
765-kV transmission corridors — one at the front entrance off CR 211 and one along the back (north)
property line adjacent to our deer breeding pens. The G31 alignment cuts through the wet-weather creek
and low-water crossing at our entry and runs through and adjacent to the ranch headquarters where seven
habitable structures and a 20,000-square-foot community building under construction are located. The G9
alignment runs through heavily treed, high-fenced wildlife habitat that has been preserved and managed for
more than 20 years under an approved Wildlife Management Plan and a Managed Lands Deer (MLD)
permit.
Both alignments impose impacts unique to a high-fenced wildlife ranch operation — including disruption
of controlled breeding programs, fawning areas, and stress-sensitive populations; breaches of fence
integrity and risk of wildlife escape, poaching, and predator intrusion; aerial-predator exposure from cleared
corridors; and interruption of harvest and hunting management. These impacts have not been considered or
quantified in the Application.
Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?
A. No.

                         PROPERTY DESCRIPTION AND LOCATION

Q. Please describe your property.
A. Jadenyx LP owns a contiguous, high-fenced family ranch in Burnet County, Texas, located along County
Road 211 near Florence. The ranch consists of six contiguous Burnet County parcels that are affected by
the proposed transmission routing. The property is our primary residence and home, and it has been
continuously used as a working ranch for more than 100 years.

Q. How is access to the property obtained?
A. Access is by a single private gated entrance off County Road 211. The entry is on Parcels 54988 and
67779 and passes through a wet-weather creek and a low-water crossing on CR 211 that floods on occasion.
The entire ranch is enclosed by high fence; gates are never left open, and fences are checked almost daily.
Q. Do you have pictures or exhibits that support your description of your property?
A. Yes. The following exhibit is referenced in my testimony and is or will be attached:

Q. Where is your property located relative to the proposed routes?
A. The property is in Burnet County, along County Road 211 near Florence. The G31 alignment crosses
the property at the front entrance corridor on the west/southwest corner, through Parcels 54987, 54988, and
67779. The G9 alignment runs just inside the north property line along the back of the ranch through Parcels
68020, 68021, and 68022, immediately adjacent to the deer breeding pens.
Q. Which routes affect your property?
A. Two proposed links affect the property: the G31 Link (affecting Burnet County Parcels 54987, 54988,
and 67779) and the G9 Link (affecting Burnet County Parcels 68020, 68021, and 68022). Together they
bracket the ranch on its front and back property lines.
Q. What routes do you oppose or support?
A. I oppose the G31 Link across Burnet County Parcels 54987, 54988, and 67779 and the G9 Link across
Burnet County Parcels 68020, 68021, and 68022. I support evaluation of less-damaging alternative
corridors that utilize existing highway, FM-road, pipeline, and previously disturbed utility rights-of-way
Direct Testimony of Vivian Kendrick
PUC Docket No. 59475
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                                   Page 5 of 14
 and that do not cross or run immediately adjacent to active MLD-permitted high-fenced wildlife habitat,
breeding pens, habitable residential structures, the in-progress community building, or the wet-weather
creek and low-water crossing at our CR 211 entrance.

                                    LAND USE AND HISTORY

Q. Please describe the history of your property and your association with it.
A. My husband and I purchased the property in 2003 from descendants of the K.L. Berry and Jester families,
who had held the land for more than 100 years. When we acquired it, the property had been heavily
overgrazed and was environmentally stressed, and the original 100-plus-year-old house needed substantial
repairs.
Through decades of substantial private investment, labor, and long-term stewardship, we have transformed
the ranch into a thriving native habitat ecosystem and a working farming and wildlife ranch. Improvements
and ongoing operations include restored native grasses and vegetation, removal of invasive species,
incubation and reintroduction of quail, increased wild turkey populations, carefully managed high-scoring
whitetail genetics and a controlled breeding program, a state-compliant Wildlife Management Plan and
active MLD permit, multiple water tanks and ponds, at least six water wells, high fencing around the entire
ranch with internal high-fenced breeding and care areas, and use of the ranch as our primary residence.
Q. How is the property currently used?
A. The property is a primary residence and a working agricultural/wildlife ranch. It is used for cattle and
wildlife management, including managed whitetail deer breeding under an MLD permit, quail and turkey
habitat management, harvesting of crops, and limited livestock. It is also used for family and community
gatherings; we are constructing an approximately 20,000-square-foot community building for home-
schooling pods, harvest sharing, and family/community events.
Q. How would the proposed transmission line affect your use of the property?
A. The G31 and G9 alignments would fundamentally interfere with how we use the property. The G31
alignment cuts through the front entrance corridor, the wet-weather creek and low-water crossing at CR
211, and the developed core of the ranch where our houses, shop, barns, breeding cooler, and community
building sit. The G9 alignment runs through high-fenced wildlife habitat at the back of the ranch
immediately adjacent to the deer breeding pens.
Construction operations — helicopter activity, blasting, heavy equipment, and ongoing maintenance traffic
— would create substantial wildlife stress conditions, with documented consequences including reduced
breeding success, altered animal-movement patterns, increased injury risk, reduced trophy antler
development, and abandonment of preferred habitat zones. Trampling through the property, reduced control
of fenced areas, and ingress/egress for construction and maintenance would jeopardize continuation of the
MLD permit and our Wildlife Management Plan.

                          COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS

Q. How does your property contribute to community values?
A. The ranch is operated as a working stewardship property: we share harvest with Feed the Hungry and
with families in need; we welcome family and friends; and we are constructing a 20,000-square-foot
Direct Testimony of Vivian Kendrick

 community building intended for home-schooling pods, harvest sharing, and family/community events. Our
family goal is to teach the next generation to live on and with the land, to be self-sufficient, and to gather
as a community.
Q. How important are views and visual character to your property?
A. Views and visual character are central to the property. Our houses sit on a hill on Parcel 67779. From
those houses, no transmission lines are visible today, and the view at sunrise is unobstructed. We moved to
the country to live with what nature provides and to enjoy that view; the visual character of the unbroken
country landscape is part of why the property has the value it does to our family and to those who visit.
Q. How would the transmission line affect the aforementioned values?
A. If the G31 Link is constructed, 765-kV towers and conductors would be in the direct line of our sunrise,
and the view from our home would be permanently degraded. The G9 Link would also be visible from our
elevated home along the back wood line. The clearing of healthy trees and wildlife habitat for either corridor
removes the meaning and feeling of living in the country, and the proposed lines are contrary to the
community values described above.

                         HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL RESOURCES

Q. Are there any archaeological sites or artifacts?
A. Yes. The surrounding area contains old Indian habitation sites and cemeteries. There are also very old
grapevines on the ranch that pre-date our ownership.
Q. Are there any historic structures or historically significant features?
A. Yes. The ranch includes the original 100-plus-year-old ranch house (now the guesthouse/ranch office),
which we have preserved and restored. The property was held by the K.L. Berry and Jester families —
well-known in University of Texas history — for more than 100 years before we purchased it in 2003. The
property has been in continuous family/ranch use for more than a century.
Q. How would the proposed routes affecting your property impact these resources?
A. Construction and corridor clearing for G31 and G9 would risk damage to or disturbance of
archaeological sites, cemeteries, and historic features in and adjacent to the proposed easements and 500-
foot setbacks. No adequate cultural-resources survey has been demonstrated for either G31 or G9 across
this property, and the visual and physical character of a century-old ranching landscape would be
permanently altered.

                                 ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY

Q. Are there environmentally sensitive areas on your property?
A. Yes. The property contains restored native grasslands and woodlands, riparian features along the wet-
weather creek at the CR 211 entrance, multiple tanks and ponds, internal water features, and heavily treed
back-of-ranch wildlife habitat preserved for wildlife use. The entire ranch is operated under an approved
Wildlife Management Plan and an active MLD permit.
Q. Are there soils, slopes, or terrain features that present environmental risk?


Direct Testimony of Vivian Kendrick
PUC Docket No. 59475
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                                    Page 7 of 14
 A. Yes. The back fence line where G9 is proposed (Parcels 68020, 68021, 68022) is rocky and hilly. The
front entry where G31 is proposed (Parcels 54988 and 67779) has a creek and low-water crossing in its
path. These site conditions increase the risk of erosion, sedimentation, and soil disturbance during and after
construction.
Q. How would the project impact environmental conditions on your property?
A. Construction and operation of the G31 and G9 corridors would fragment carefully managed habitat
systems and reverse decades of environmental restoration. Corridor clearing, access roads, and tower
foundations associated with a 765-kV line will remove mature trees, native vegetation, and ground cover
that have taken more than 20 years to restore.
Cleared corridors also create open aerial lanes that increase exposure of quail, turkey, fawns, and other
ground-nesting wildlife to aerial and ground predators, altering predator-prey dynamics that have taken
decades to stabilize through habitat management.

                             WATER RESOURCES AND FLOODING

Q. Have you observed flooding on your property?
A. Yes. The wet-weather creek and low-water crossing at the CR 211 entrance — within the G31 alignment
on Parcels 54988 and 67779 — floods on occasion. Both the G31 and G9 alignments cross or border ponds,
tank drainages, and flood-prone areas on the property.
Q. Are there creeks, springs, wetlands, or seeps present?
A. Yes. There is a wet-weather creek at the front entrance corridor (G31), plus numerous tanks, ponds, and
tank drainages across the ranch. We have restored creeks and water features over more than 20 years, and
the property includes riparian features that support native wildlife.
Q. How do you think construction for this type of project could impact drainage or flooding?
A. Construction in and around the CR 211 creek and low-water crossing will worsen flooding, drainage,
and erosion at our entry, and will introduce sediment into the creek and downstream tanks. Heavy
equipment, access roads, matting, fill, and tower foundations within the easement will alter natural drainage
patterns, and the cumulative effect of clearing along both G31 and G9 alignments will increase runoff and
sediment transport over the lifespan of the line.

                            WATER SUPPLY AND GROUNDWATER

Q. Do you rely on groundwater wells?
A. Yes. Groundwater from wells is our sole source of water on the property. There are at least six water
wells on the ranch, supporting our residences, the community building under construction, livestock and
wildlife water systems, and our agricultural operations.
Q. Are there stock ponds or stock tanks on the property?
A. Yes. We have multiple stock tanks and ponds across the ranch that we have built and maintained as part
of our wildlife and livestock water systems and habitat management program.
Q. What risks do you anticipate this project could pose to your water supply?

Direct Testimony of Vivian Kendrick
PUC Docket No. 59475
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                                    Page 8 of 14
 A. We are concerned that construction activity, blasting, and corridor clearing within the G31 and G9
alignments could affect groundwater recharge, water seepage to wells and ponds, and water quality, and
that sedimentation from the G31 creek crossing could degrade downstream tanks. The Application has not
addressed these site-specific groundwater and surface-water impacts.

                                 AGRICULTURAL OPERATIONS

Q. What agricultural or land management activities occur on your property?
A. The ranch is a high-fenced wildlife ranch and working farming and hunting ranch operated under an
MLD permit and an approved Wildlife Management Plan. Activities include managed whitetail deer
breeding and harvest; quail incubation, reintroduction, and habitat management; turkey nesting habitat
management; native-vegetation restoration and invasive-species removal; multiple tanks, ponds, and water
systems; and managed harvest shared with families in need and Feed the Hungry. We also have internal
high-fenced breeding and care areas for stress-sensitive populations.
Q. Are there seasonal operations, such as calving, harvesting, and/or hunting?
A. Yes. Seasonal operations include fawning and breeding seasons for managed whitetail deer, quail and
turkey nesting seasons, planting and harvest cycles, hunting seasons, and required whitetail harvest
management under the MLD permit.
Q. How would construction interfere with these operations?
A. Construction and maintenance operations could severely interfere with hunting seasons, guided wildlife
activities, harvest schedules, breeding periods, and wildlife movement patterns. Disruption of required
whitetail-harvest management directly impacts wildlife-population obligations under the MLD permit,
ranch economics, and our long-standing sharing of harvest with Feed the Hungry and with families in need.
Any approval should at a minimum require that construction and maintenance ingress and egress avoid
hunting seasons and breeding periods, and that the State or the applicant maintain the integrity and security
of the high fence during construction.

                   ENGINEERING, ACCESS, AND CONSTRUCTABILITY

Q. Are there limitations to accessing your property?
A. Yes. The entire ranch is enclosed by high fence and accessed by a single private gated entrance off CR
211. Gates are never left open, fences are checked almost daily, and there are internal high-fenced breeding
and care areas with their own access controls. Any construction access to the G31 or G9 alignments will
require fence breaches and controlled entry.
Q. Are there terrain or soil constraints?
A. Yes. The back fence line where G9 is proposed is rocky and hilly. The front entry where G31 is proposed
has a wet-weather creek and low-water crossing in its path. These site conditions present constraints for
heavy 765-kV tower foundations and for access roads, matting, and staging.
Q. Are there conflicts with existing infrastructure?
A. There are no existing transmission lines on the property today. We have only a distribution line to a pole
near our home from CR 211 and service lines from that pole to our various buildings. The perimeter and
Direct Testimony of Vivian Kendrick

 internal high fencing, the gated CR 211 entrance, multiple water wells and water lines, and the in-progress
20,000-square-foot community building all represent existing infrastructure that would conflict with
corridor construction.
Q. How do you think the soil constraints and existing infrastructure could affect the construction,
maintenance, or safety of these lines?
A. Rocky, hilly soils along the G9 alignment and the creek/low-water crossing along the G31 alignment
increase erosion, sedimentation, and stability risks during and after construction. Heavy 765-kV tower
foundations in these conditions create long-term soil-stability concerns. Construction in and around our
high fence, water wells, and water lines creates risk of damage and security breaches, and the community
building under construction will be in proximity to construction activity, which raises safety concerns
during construction.

                PRUDENT AVOIDANCE AND HABITABLE STRUCTURES

Q. Please describe all habitable structures on your property.
A. There are seven habitable structures plus a 20,000-square-foot community building under construction
on the ranch headquarters tract (Parcel 67779), with another family home in final architectural planning:
1. Main ranch house — approximately 6,000 square feet, 5 bedrooms, 3 baths, with three additions made
over 22 years.
2. Guesthouse/ranch office — the original 100-plus-year-old house, 3 bedrooms, office, 2 baths.
3. “Man Cave” with bathroom, 2-car garage, and RV garage.
4. Shop/warehouse with walk-in animal hanging cooler.
5. Work barn/warehouse.
6. Feed warehouse / pole barn for large equipment.
7. Two-bedroom cabin.
Under construction: approximately 20,000-square-foot community building (roof being installed now),
intended for home-schooling pods and family/community events.
Planned: an additional family home in final architectural design.
Q. Are there any habitable structures within 500 feet of the proposed centerline?
A. Yes. The 500-foot setback area associated with the G31 alignment covers portions of Parcel 67779 where
habitable structures sit. The G31 alignment enters the property at the CR 211 entrance and approaches the
developed core of the ranch from the west, placing habitable structures within the 500-foot setback band.
Q. Beyond the home itself, are there outdoor living areas, ranch structures, or work areas affected
by the proposed centerline?
A. Yes. The ranch headquarters tract (Parcel 67779) contains the shop with walk-in animal cooler, the work
barn, the feed warehouse/pole barn, the two-bedroom cabin, the Man Cave/garage complex, the in-progress
community building, and the outdoor entertaining and gathering areas where we host family and


Direct Testimony of Vivian Kendrick
PUC Docket No. 59475
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                                 Page 10 of 14
 community. The internal high-fenced breeding pens on Parcels 68020, 68021, and 68022 are immediately
adjacent to the G9 alignment.
Q. How close are the proposed routes to these structures?
A. The G31 alignment enters the property at the CR 211 front entrance corridor and approaches the ranch
headquarters from the west, with the 500-foot setback band overlapping habitable structures on Parcel
67779. The G9 alignment runs just inside the north property line on Parcels 68020, 68021, and 68022,
immediately adjacent to the deer breeding pens. Both alignments are visible from the elevated hilltop on
which our houses sit.
Q. What areas of your property are most actively used?
A. The most actively used areas are the ranch headquarters core on Parcel 67779 (residences, guesthouse,
garages, shop/cooler, barns, cabin, community building site, and surrounding entertaining and outdoor
living areas) and the high-fenced internal breeding pens at the back of the ranch on Parcels 68020, 68021,
and 68022, which we work daily.
Q. Does the current route placement require you to move any existing structures or hinder your
ability to build planned structures?
A. Yes. The G31 alignment’s 500-foot setback band overlaps the ranch headquarters core and would hinder
the planned additional family home that is currently in final architectural design and the further build-out
of the community building campus. The G9 alignment immediately adjacent to internal high-fenced
breeding pens would constrain expansion and ongoing use of those breeding facilities.

Q. Based on your testimony, do any of the routes involving your property best meet the statutory
criteria of considering community values, environmental integrity, and/or land use compatibility?

(fragmenting restored habitat, crossing a wet-weather creek and low-water crossing, and creating predator-
exposure corridors), and land-use compatibility (running through the developed ranch headquarters core
and immediately adjacent to internal high-fenced breeding pens on an MLD-permitted property).
Q. What action would you like the Commission to take?
A. I respectfully request that the Commission:
(1) deny inclusion ofthe G31 Link across Bumet County Parcels 54987,54988, and 67779;

FM-road, pipeline, and previously disturbed utility corridors and that do not cross or run immediately
adjacent to active MLD-permitted high-fenced wildlife habitat, breeding pens, habitable residential
structures, the in-progress community building, or the wet-weather creek and low-water crossing at the CR
211 entrance;

roads, staging areas, fence-breach plans, restoration obligations, and impacts to MLD/Wildlife
Management Plan compliance, before approving any alignment across the Jadenyx LP property; and

(5) require a structure-by-structure setback and EMF analysis at habitable structures, and a hydrology,
erosion, and water-quality analysis at the CR 211 low-water crossing, if any portion of the alignment
remains under consideration.
